gloss: the language of the article corrected

form: In the article “The Exponence and Development of Plurals in Nuuchahnulth” by David Inman (Papers for ICSNL 56:111–133), there was an error on page 125, which the author wishes to correct.

gloss: page 1, ‘size’, the base of the adjectives

form: The plural forms for the adjectives based on ʔanaḥ ‘size’ are not irregular, as stated in the article, but formed in part through a phonological rule which includes the “thinning” of prenasal vowels to i. The process is described in greatest detail in Davidson 2002:19–23, with the example of ʔanaḥ given on p. 210. The result of the full phonological process is that a sequence of CVNV (where N is any nasal) becomes CiN.

gloss: page 1, CV- reduplication, then the thinning of CVNV to CiN; the middle form starred, unattested
page 1, unobserved, CV- reduplication applied before the infix
page 1, ‘boys’, Barkley Sound, the only fully irregular plural left in the article
page 1, the underlying form of meʔiƛqac

form: The formation of the plural of ʔanaḥʔis is normal CV- reduplication followed by “thinning” of CVNV to CiN: ʔanaḥʔis > * ʔaʔanaḥʔis > ʔaʔinḥʔis. Interestingly, the infixed <čk> must be inserted after reduplication, as application of CV- reduplication to ʔačknaḥ would yield the unobserved *ʔaʔačknaḥ, which would not feed into the thinning rule. This correction means that the only fully irregular plural in the paper is Barkley Sound maaƛʔitqinḥ ‘boys’ from meʔiƛqac ‘boy’ (underlying, maʔiƛqac).
